聚陽 (1477 TT) 
最壞情況已過，接單表現應逐步回升

永豐觀點 
原油價格維持高檔，地緣政治風險仍存，造成品牌商下單信心保守，考量客戶庫存
水位已低，拉貨力道有望逐步回溫，聚陽營運谷底應已過，評價有望逐步好轉，研
究部對聚陽營運看法維持正向。 
 投資評價與建議 
投資建議維持買進，目標價 258 元：受原物料價格高漲及戰爭影響，客戶下單態
度趨於保守，考量目前客戶庫存水位已低，公司最壞情況應已過，隨著戰爭及原物
料等風險因素解除，聚陽客戶下單信心有望逐步恢復， 惟短期客戶仍未進入補庫存
循環 ， 將抑制聚陽獲利成長動能 ， 預估公司2026/2027 稅後 EPS 15.77/17.18 元，
公司過去四年股利配發率皆達 99%以上，以此推估公司 2027 年配息，殖利率應
達 8%以上，具備殖利率保護，目前本益比處於歷史區間近最下緣，考量公司營運
谷底已過，評價應逐步回升，給予本益比15X，目標價258 元，投資建議維持買進。

ESG 評析 
聚陽企業永續評鑑整體為 B+等，於 SASB 產業永續議題與跨產業五大永續面向平
均得分分別為 B 等與 A 等。 
SinoPac+ ESG 評鑑系統評等

聚陽為亞太地區知名成衣製造商：公司設立於 1990 年，主要業務包括成衣設計、
製造與銷售，主要原料包括主料（本布）及副料（拉鍊等），以向國內外知名廠商
下單為主。公司目前主要生產地區包含越南、印尼、柬埔寨、中國、孟加拉、薩爾
瓦多，2025 年公司主要客戶營收比重：GAP 占 36%，T arget占 18%，日系客戶
占 18%，Dick′s Sporting goods 占 9%，Kohl′s 占 7%，其他占 12%。 
3Q26 獲利預期季增：聚陽 8 月營收 35.6 億元(+18.5% MoM，-5.1% YoY)，符
合預期。聚陽 8M26 出貨量-12% YoY，價持平 YoY，匯率影響+7% YoY。展望
3Q26，受戰爭及通膨因素影響，客戶下單態度趨於保守，提高短交期訂單比重，
聚陽 3Q26 短單比重提升至 15%，出貨量預期年增約中個位數，ASP 受產品組合
影響而預期年減約 3%，研究部預估聚陽 3Q26 營收 96.4 億元，（+18.1％QoQ，
+8.5％ YoY） ，預估毛利率24.03%，（+0.16 pts. QoQ，+2.12 pts. YoY） ，預估
稅後淨利 10.5 億元（+18.1％ QoQ，+8.5％ YoY） ，稅後EPS 4.26 元。 
獲利表現穩健，維持買進投資建議：展望後市，客戶下單仍趨於保守，聚陽 4Q26
短交期訂單比重預期將達 15-20%，預期 4Q26 出貨量將年增低個位數，ASP 因
公司挑單生產及因應原物料報價調漲 ， 預期將年增5-7%， 取決於短交期訂單比重 。
公司計畫於 2027 年持續擴增印尼及孟加拉產能，2027 年聚陽整體產能預期將年
增約 7-8%，若客戶補庫存力道較預期積極，則有望提升至雙位數以上增長。研究
部評估聚陽受到原物料價格高漲及戰爭影響， 客戶下單態度趨於保守， 聚陽短單比
重已由先前約 10%提升至 15%，考量目前客戶庫存水位已低，公司最壞情況應已
過，隨著戰爭及原物料等風險因素解除，聚陽客戶下單信心有望逐步恢復，惟短期
客戶仍未進入補庫存循環，將抑制聚陽獲利成長動能。綜合以上，研究部預估公司
2026 年營收 356.1 億元（+3.4％ YoY），毛利率 25.39%，稅後淨利 38.9 億元
（+7.6％YoY） ，稅後EPS 15.77 元。預估公司 2027 年營收 384.7 億元（+8.0％ 
YoY） ，毛利率25.46%，稅後淨利 42.4 億元 （+9.0％YoY） ，稅後EPS 17.18 元，
公司過去四年股利配發率皆達 99%以上，以此推估公司 2027 年配息，殖利率應
達 8%以上，具備殖利率保護，聚陽目前本益比處於歷史區間近最下緣，考量公司
營運谷底已過，評價應逐步回升，給予本益比 15X，目標價 258 元，投資建議維
持買進。

投資評等  強力買進

士電(1503)  
目標價位  250 元

獲利成長至 2028 年無虞

公司治理評鑑排序： 
1 2 3 4 5 6 7

個股基本資料：

徐培勛 
鋼鐵、重電產業 
S1120023@tss-c.com.tw 
 股價評價基礎： 
AI、半導體帶動用電需求激增，士電已接獲客戶需求，重電 T4 廠產能將於
4Q27 量產 ，2H28 開始貢獻營收 ；2027~2028 進入表後儲能工程認列高峰 ，
預估 2026/2027/2028 稅後 淨利 YoY+29%/+33%/+15% ， 稅 後EPS 
8.10/10.80/12.46 元，給予強力買進評等，目標價 250 元(20x 2028 EPS)，
潛在漲幅 22%。

營運近況摘要： 
士電成立於 1955 年，為台灣老牌變壓器生產商，技術來自三菱重工的技轉，
1H26 產品組合：電力配電(變壓器、配電盤)72%、車輛零件 15%、自動化設
備(工具機)10%、其他 3%。內外銷比 65%：35%。客戶包含：Mitsubishi 
Electric/Mitsuba Electric/ Panasonic/ Hitachi ABB/ Siemens/泓德能源/起
而行/和泰車。目前三個廠區都在新竹：電裝廠、新豐廠及重電廠。

2026 年重電 T1+T2 廠產能利用率提升，T3 廠、表後儲能小幅貢獻 
預估 2026 年營收 415 億元(YoY+12%)，因變壓器需求殷切，重電 T1、T2
廠產能利用率提升至 90%，重電 T3 廠 2025/9 開始量產，Lead time 1~1.5
年，4Q26 開始認列營收，2027 年全面貢獻；且公司在手 500MW 表後儲能
(太陽能儲能)統包案也開始貢獻營收 ； 毛利率21%(YoY+0.2ppts)， 因產品組
合較同期相同； 業外則有 金融資產 公允價值、匯兌利益挹注，稅後淨利
YoY+29%，稅後 EPS 8.15 元。

2027~2028 年 T3、T4 廠產能提升，表後儲能進入認列高峰 
展望 2027~2028 年，重電內銷(佔重電 80%)：政府希望強韌電網計畫完工
期限從 2033 年提早至 2028 年，依 2027 年預算書依然維持 2033 年完工，
2026/2027/2028 資本支出 46/118/155 億元，維持成長態勢。重電外銷(佔
重電 20%)： 為了因應全球 AI、半導體等強勁用電需求，重電 T4 廠將於
2027/9 量產，預期2H28 開始貢獻營收，2029 年全面貢獻，T1+T2 年產能
10GVA(十億伏安)，T3 可貢獻產能 5GVA、T4 再貢獻 5GVA，T4 主要客戶
為日本、美國電力市場，並專注在 345KV 變壓器生產。國內表後儲能(太陽
能)：公司在手 500MW 表後儲能案，若假設 2026/2027/2028 完工比率
10%/40%/50%計算，預計貢獻 7.5/30/37.5 億元，

表二、股利政策表

投資評等定義如下 
強力買進：預估未來 1 年內目標價格和收盤價格差距+20%以上

營收走勢圖

玻璃陶瓷–電子材料  
富喬(1815.TT) 
AI 材料升級趨勢確立，高階玻纖布開啟成長新局

富喬為台灣少數具備紗、布垂直整合與自有配方能力的玻纖布廠。2H26 
受惠二代低介電布放量、報價調漲及良率改善，營收與 獲利可望逐季創
高；進入 2027 年後，獲利成長動能將由高階產品占比提升與新增產能
貢獻。台灣廠持續將既有產能轉向二代低介電布，東莞廠自 1Q27 起分
批將 E 布產能升級至二代布，泰國一期則自 2H27 起逐步投產，承接
客戶對非中國高階產能的需求，加上低膨脹布開始導入，產品組合將進
一步往高階化發展。研究部預估富喬 2026、2027 年稅後 EPS 分別為 
5.13 元與 9.30 元，稅後淨利分別年增 267.9% 與 81.4%。考量富喬
為日系龍頭以外少數具備垂直整合與自有配方能力的供應商，以  2027 
年獲利為評價基礎，給予 20 倍本益比，目標價 185 元，初次給予買進
投資評等。

1. 規格升級推動產品組合高階化 
AI 伺服器與高速交換器的傳輸速率持續提升 ， 板材由 M7、M8 向 M9 以
上升級，玻纖布同步由 E-glass 轉向一代、二代低介電布。石英布因鑽
孔與除膠渣良率受限而導入遞延，終端客戶轉回採用二代低介電布，延
長其產品週期。研究部預估富喬二代低介電布營收占比將由 2025 年的 
7%，提升至 2026 年的 27% 與 2027 年的 51%。

2. 既有機台重新配置，毛利率大幅跳升 
玻纖布織布機由豐田獨家供應 ， 新機交期已排至 2031 年，2027 年以前
產業新增供給主要仰賴既有機台重新配置 。 富喬現有約 920 台織機 ， 憑
藉紗、布垂直整合，可在無須大幅增加資本支出下將既有產能轉向二代
低介電布 ， 帶動毛利率由 2025 年的 27.6%， 升至 2026 年的 44.7% 與 
2027 年的 54.8%。

### Page 2

請參見末頁重要披露及免責聲明 2

公司簡介 
富喬工業（1815 TT）成立於 1999 年，為台灣少數具備玻璃纖維紗至玻璃纖
維布垂直整合能力的材料廠，主要產品涵蓋電子級、工業級玻纖紗及電子級玻
纖布，其中電子級玻纖布為銅箔基板（CCL）與印刷電路板（PCB）的關鍵上游
材料。公司目前主要生產基地位於雲林斗六、虎尾及中國東莞，並已布局泰國
新產能，以強化非中國供應鏈配置。相較單純織布廠，富喬具備自有玻纖紗生
產與配方研發能力，可依終端規格變化調整紗種與產品組合。近年受惠 AI 伺
服器、高速交換器等應用帶動 PCB 材料規格持續升級，富喬營運重心逐步由
傳統 E-glass 轉向低介電等高階電子級材料。

玻纖布產業介紹 
玻纖布位於 PCB 材料供應鏈最上游，製程橫跨玻璃熔煉與紡織兩個領域。玻
纖原料經窯爐熔融後 ， 由鉑銠漏板拉製成單絲 ， 再經上漿 、 集束與加撚形成電
子紗 ， 後續以織機織成玻纖布 ， 並經開纖及矽烷偶聯劑等後處理後 ， 交由 CCL 
廠含浸樹脂製成膠片，再與銅箔壓合成銅箔基板，最終應用於 PCB 或載板。 
玻纖布規格主要可由織物型號 、 紗徑與玻璃配方三個面向區分 。 以織物型號而
言，7628 屬厚布，基重約 210 g/m²，2116、1080 依序變薄，10 系列則屬超
薄布；若依紗徑區分，粗紗單纖直徑約 9 至 13 微米，細紗則降至約 4 至 
9 微米，隨紗徑變細，斷絲風險與製程難度同步提高，織機亦須降速，超薄布
生產效率僅約厚布的二分之一至三分之一 。 另一方面 ， 玻璃配方則直接決定材
料電性 ， 介電損耗亦隨材料世代持續下降 。 隨高速傳輸規格提升 ，玻纖與樹脂
之間的介電差異會放大訊號時延與織紋效應 ， 因此傳輸速率每提升一個世代 ，
材料亦須同步升級。 
除玻璃配方外，織布後的開纖與表面處理亦是高階玻纖布性能的關鍵。即使
CCL 廠商採用相同原料，不同玻纖布廠的產品在電性、耐熱性與良率上的表現
仍可能存在顯著差異，也使高階玻纖布認證週期通常長達兩年以上。就材料成
本結構而言，玻纖布占傳統 CCL 材料成本約 25% 至 40%，若升級至石英布，
占比可提高至約六成；隨高階 PCB 對 CCL 規格與用量提升，CCL 占 PCB 用
料成本比重亦由過去三至四成提升至五成以上。玻纖布因此已由過去的通用材
料，逐步轉變為影響高速板材性能、成本與供應穩定性的關鍵材料。

富喬為台灣少數具備玻纖紗、布
垂直整合與自有配方能力的材料
廠，近年受惠 AI 帶動高階 PCB 
材料升級 ， 營運重心正由傳統 E-
glass 轉向低介電玻纖布，並同
步布局泰國非中國產能。

玻纖布位於 PCB 材料供應鏈最
上游 ， 製程與認證門檻高 ， 且隨高
速傳輸推升材料規格升級，其成
本占比與對板材性能的重要性同
步提升，已由通用材料轉為高階  
PCB 的關鍵材料。

### Page 4

請參見末頁重要披露及免責聲明 4

AI 世代推升高速材料規格持續升級 
AI 基礎建設對材料的需求，並非僅來自伺服器出貨量成長，更重要的是運算
密度與傳輸速率持續提升，帶動 PCB 材料規格同步升級。相較傳統伺服器約
三至四年的平台週期，AI 伺服器迭代速度明顯加快，GPU、ASIC 與交換器間
的資料傳輸需求快速增加，推動網路架構由 400G、800G 向 1.6T、3.2T 演
進。隨訊號速率提升，傳輸損耗與訊號完整性要求同步提高，板材須持續降低
介電常數與介電損耗，帶動 CCL 由 M7、M8 向 M9 以上升級；玻纖布作為影
響板材電性的重要材料，亦由傳統 E-glass 逐步升級至一代、二代低介電
布，並進一步朝石英布與第三代低介電材料發展。 
就目前材料演進路徑而言，400G 交換器主要採用 M7 板材搭配一代低介電
布，800G 升級至 M8 後，一代與二代低介電布開始並用；進入 1.6T 世代
後，二代低介電布的重要性進一步提升，部分高階規格則開始評估導入石英
布。展望 2028 年後，隨 3.2T 逐步導入，材料規格預期將進一步朝升級版石
英布或第三代低介電布發展，高階玻纖布的滲透率持續提升。 
研究部認為，規格升級將成為本輪玻纖布產業成長的核心驅動力。隨 AI 運算
與高速傳輸規格持續演進，材料需求將由傳統 E-glass 加速轉向低介電、低
膨脹等高階產品。在終端平台持續更替的背景下，玻纖布須隨板材世代同步升
級，而每一次規格提升亦伴隨 ASP 與單位產值增加，使產業成長不僅來自需
求量擴張，更來自產品組合持續高階化。

### Page 5

請參見末頁重要披露及免責聲明 5

專利與認證構成高階玻纖布的實質進入障礙 
高階玻纖布的核心技術門檻在玻纖紗配方，低介電與低膨脹材料的關鍵專利亦
主要集中於紗端，後進者若要切入，須重新設計配方以迴避既有專利，良率與
量產時程因而受限。另一方面，CCL 廠需將特定玻纖布與樹脂、銅箔共同調
校，一旦納入合格供應商名單，更換材料通常須重新開立料號並進行完整驗
證，使認證週期可長達數年。富喬憑藉紗、布垂直整合，可直接由紗端調整配
方與製程，並已完成多地高階低介電玻纖布專利布局，低膨脹布亦已突破既有
專利限制並通過終端認證。研究部認為專利保護與長認證週期共同構成高階玻
纖布的實質進入障礙，亦使中國廠商產能雖快速擴張，短期內能實際轉化為高
階產品供給的比例仍有限。

供需失衡與料源綁定 
玻纖布供需失衡自 2026 年起由通用布延伸至高階布，主要瓶頸集中於織機、
良率與認證。玻纖布織機由豐田獨家供應，新機交期已排至 2031 年，且超薄
與特殊布須降速生產，使名目機台數無法等比轉化為實際產出；另一方面，高
階布認證週期普遍超過兩年，也使既有產能難以在短期內快速切換料號。 
E 布短缺主要來自龍頭廠商退出低階產能。日東紡、旭化成陸續停產 E-glass 
布後，供給收縮帶動各類 E 布報價自 2025 年底至 2026 年普遍上漲逾一倍
以上。惟中國新增產能自 2027 年陸續開出，加上消費性需求仍偏弱，研究部
預期 E 布供需將於 2027 年逐步緩解，報價漲幅趨緩。 
一代低介電布供需相對平衡，惟隨二代布需求放大，具備雙線能力的廠商傾向
將織機轉向二代布。二代低介電布則為目前供給最為吃緊的品項，主要對應 
M8 以上板材。除織機供給受限外，良率更是限制有效產出的關鍵，新進者量
產良率多不足五成，使名目產能與實際出貨量存在明顯落差，也支撐二代布報
價維持在一代布的約 2 至 3 倍。 
低膨脹布的供給缺口則可能延續更久。隨先進封裝尺寸放大與層數增加，而供
應仍高度集中於日東紡，新產能最快自 2H27 起陸續開出。石英布則面臨不同
瓶頸，問題不在供給，而在加工良率與導入進度；由於鑽孔與除膠渣難度較
高，部分原規劃採用石英布的設計轉回二代低介電布，反而延長二代布的產品
週期。 
供給吃緊亦同步改變材料認證與採購模式。過去玻纖布多由 CCL 廠與板廠選
料，現階段雲端業者與系統廠已逐步直接認證布廠並指定料源，部分客戶另要
求非中國產能，CCL 廠亦透過長約提前鎖定高階布供給。高階玻纖布的競爭因
而由單純產能擴張，轉向認證、良率與料源掌握能力的競爭。

高階玻纖布具備配方專利與長認
證週期雙重門檻，限制新進者有
效產能釋放，也使富喬憑藉紗布
垂直整合與既有認證基礎建立明
顯競爭優勢。

玻纖布供給受限於織機、良率與
認證門檻，高階產品短缺延續並
推動客戶直接綁定料源，產業競
爭 重 心 由 產 能 擴 張 轉 向 認 證 能
力、量產良率與供應穩定性。

### Page 6

請參見末頁重要披露及免責聲明 6

圖三、二代低介電布供需缺口

資料來源：統一投顧預估

產能配置與產品組合 
富喬目前共有約 920 台織布機，其中台灣 490 台、東莞 430 台。受限於織
布機交期，富喬 2027 年以前的主要成長動能，是將既有機台由 E 布、一代
低介電布持續轉向單位產值與毛利率更高的二代低介電布，透過產品組合升級
放大既有產能效益。 
台灣廠部分機台維持生產 E 布，供應台系 CCL 廠與低軌衛星應用，其餘產能
則持續轉向二代低介電布，低膨脹布亦預計自 2027 年起逐步導入。海外方
面，東莞現有 430 台於 2026 年仍以 E 布為主，自 1Q27 起採台灣供紗、當
地織布模式分批轉作二代低介電布。泰國一期則規劃新增 500 台織機，預計
自 2H27 起分批到位，主要生產低介電布並承接客戶對非中國產能的需求。 
富喬能快速進行跨廠區與跨產品配置，關鍵在於紗、布垂直整合。公司自有電
子級玻纖紗可隨布種升級同步調整紗的配方與規格，降低對外部紗源的依賴。
隨台灣產能持續高階化、東莞轉產二代布及泰國新產能加入，研究部預估二代
低介電布營收占比將由 2025 年的 7%，提升至 2026 年的 27% 與 2027 年的 
51%，同期毛利率亦由 27.6% 升至 44.7% 與 54.8%。

富喬以既有機台轉產高毛利二代
低介電布，並透過東莞轉線與泰
國新產能擴充高階產品供給，帶
動二代布營收占比與整體毛利率
持續提升。

圖四、富喬產品組合演變（營收占比）

資料來源：統一投顧預估

營運概況 
1. 2H26 營運將改寫新高 
富喬 7、8 月營收分別為 8.54 億元（+24.0% MoM、+68.1% YoY）與 9.12 億
元（+6.8% MoM、+79.2% YoY） ，連續改寫單月新高。隨新一代 AI 伺服器與 
1.6T 交換器平台陸續放量，二代低介電布需求同步攀升，加以 6 月起調漲的
報價自 3Q26 全季認列，研究部預估 3Q26 營收 27.66 億元（+29.8% QoQ、
+80.4% YoY） ，改寫單季歷史新高。毛利率升至 48.8%（+8.8ppt QoQ、
+21.9ppt YoY） ，除產品組合與報價效益外，二代布量產良率亦已逐步改善。
營業利益 10.39 億元（+89.8% QoQ、+301.5% YoY） ，營益率 37.6%；稅後淨
利 8.58 億元（+1.8% QoQ、+203.2% YoY），EPS 1.40 元，EPS 較 2Q26 小幅
下滑係因盈餘轉增資後股數增加。展望 4Q26，隨著二代布出貨比重持續提升
以及良率續揚貢獻，研究部預估營收 30.51 億元（+10.3% QoQ、+86.4% 
YoY） 、毛利率 49.9%、EPS 1.62 元。

2. 2027 年成長動能轉向產品組合升級，EPS 估 9.30 元 
2027 年富喬獲利成長動能將由價格上漲轉向產品組合升級與新增產能貢獻。
台灣廠持續將既有機台由一代轉向二代低介電布，東莞廠自 1Q27 起採台灣供
紗、當地織布模式，分批將 E 布產能轉作二代布；泰國一期則自 2H27 起逐
步投產，主要承接客戶對非中國高階產能的需求。隨三地產能同步往高階產品
配置，研究部預估二代低介電布營收占比將由 2026 年的 27% 提升至 2027 
年的 51%，成為獲利成長的主要來源。研究部預估 2027 年營收 149.82 億元
（+52.4% YoY） ，並隨泰國產能開出及二代布占比提升呈逐季成長；毛利率升
至 54.8%，營益率達 45.7%，帶動稅後淨利 57.18 億元（+81.4% YoY），EPS 
9.30 元。

2H26 受惠二代低介電布需求放
量 、 漲價效益與良率改善 ， 富喬營
收與毛利率同步攀升，研究部預
期 3Q26、4Q26 營運將連續改寫
新高。

2027 年富喬成長動能將由漲價
轉 向 產 品 組 合 升 級 與 新 產 能 貢
獻 ， 隨台灣 、 東莞及泰國產能加速
轉向二代低介電布，研究部預估
二代布營收占比升至 51%，帶動 
EPS 成長至 9.30 元。

投資建議 
研究部初次給予富喬買進投資評等，主要考量：(1) 石英布受鑽孔損耗與加
工良率限制 ， 導入時程遞延 ， 終端客戶轉回採用二代低介電布搭配高階樹脂的
架構，延長二代布產品週期，帶動富喬二代低介電布營收占比由 2025 年的 
7%，提升至 2026 年的 27% 與 2027 年的 51%；(2) 玻纖布織布機由豐田獨
家供應，目前新機交期已排至 2031 年，意味 2027 年以前產業新增供給主
要仰賴既有機台重新配置 ， 富喬可在無須大幅增加資本支出的情況下 ， 持續將
既有產能由 E 布轉向一代及二代低介電布，研究部推算二代布毛利率較一代
布高逾 10 個百分點，產品組合優化將推升毛利率由 2025 年的 27.6%，提
升至 2026 年的 44.7% 與 2027 年的 54.8%；(3) 東莞廠自 1Q27 起採台灣
供紗、當地織布模式，分批將既有產能轉作二代低介電布，泰國一期則規劃  
500 台織機，自 2H27 起逐步開出，同樣以低介電布為主要產品，並承接客
戶對非中國產能的需求 。綜上所述 ， 研究部預估富喬 2026、2027 年稅後 EPS 
分別為 5.13 元與 9.30 元，稅後純益分別年增 267.9% 與 81.4%。考量富
喬為日系龍頭以外少數具備紗、布垂直整合與自有配方 能力的供應商，以  
2027 年獲利為評價基礎，給予 20 倍本益比，目標價 185 元，初次給予買
進投資評等。

評等  定義  
強力買進     預估未來 6 個月內的絕對報酬超過 25%以上

電子–通信網路  
全新(2455.TT) 
產能不是問題，基板供應改善推升營收獲利成長

研究部初次給予全新買進建議，主因為：(1)InP 基板供應改善帶
動光電子快速放量，且高毛利光電子占比由 1H26 約 26%提升至 7 月
40%、8 月 46.1%，光電子超越微電子的黃金交叉將近；(2)產品組合轉
佳 、 較高毛利的客供料占比逐步提升及價格調整效益帶動獲利改善 ， 管
理層預期 3Q26 毛利率可回升至 40%以上；(3)展望 2027 年，美系客戶
200G PD 預計 1Q27 開始明顯放量，CW Laser 及 EML 發射端則接續放
量，管理層預期2027 年發射端營收有望超越接收端。綜上所述，研究
部預估全新2026/2027 營收為49.02/78.77 億元 ， 分別年增45%/60.7%，
EPS 分別為 6.08/11.63 元，評價方面，考量目前上游磊晶需求持續強
勁，且基板供應逐步改善有望帶動營收獲利成長，因此給予60 倍本益
比，目標價 700 元(60PER*2027EPS)。

1. 3Q26 基板供貨穩定帶動高毛利光電子營收佔比提升 
研究部預估3Q26 營收將季增 44.2%達13.92 億元，EPS 為1.69 元，
主係:(1)基板供應穩定加上客戶自行攜帶基板數量增加；(2)高毛
利光電子營收佔比持續提升 。 預估毛利率達42.3%， 季增3.7ppts，
短期營運動能持續向上。

2. MOCVD 產能持續擴充，產能不成問題，2027 年光電子成長可期 
7 月整體MOCVD 稼動率僅約 50%，2027 年GaAs 及InP 共用的MOCVD
機台數新增至 66 台，後續有望隨 InP 需求，調整成 InP 產能使
用，滿足光電子產品後續需求。展望 2027 年，接收端 200G PD 於
1Q27 開始放量，發射端 CW Laser 及 EML 於 1H27 開始量產，且發
射端有望超越接收端，成為 2027 年光電子營收成長動能。

公司簡介 
全新光電（2455）成立於1996 年，為全球主要Ⅲ-V 族化合物半導體專業磊
晶廠，以MOCVD（金屬有機化學氣相沉積）為核心技術，主要提供客戶磊晶
晶圓 ， 產品可分為微電子及光電子兩大領域 。 微電子產品以GaAs HBT、PHEMT
等磊晶片為主，主要應用於手機、Wi-Fi、基地台等射頻功率放大器 （PA），
目前為全球最大 GaAs PA 磊晶供應商；光電子產品則涵蓋 InGaAs PD/APD、
FP/DFB Laser 及 VCSEL 等磊晶片，應用於光通訊、資料中心、LiDAR 及感測
等市場。2Q26 產品組合為微電子 73%、光電子 27%。

圖一、全新 2Q26 營收佔比

資料來源：全新，統一投顧整理

產業概況 
(1) 手機進入成長高原期，WiFi7/8 與新興終端擴大GaAs 應用場景 
GaAs憑藉高頻、高線性度及高功率效率等特性，長期為無線通訊RF前端的
重要材料，主要應用於PA、LNA及部分Switch，其中HBT仍為手機與WiFi PA
的主流技術。過去GaAs需求主要隨智慧型手機通訊規格升級而成長，隨4G
進入5G後，新增頻段使PA數量及RF前端複雜度同步提升，5G手機所需GaAs
磊晶面積約較4G增加20%～30%，帶動單機GaAs價值持續提高。

然而，隨全球智慧型手機市場逐步成熟，未來GaAs需求成長動能將由過去
依賴手機出貨量增加 ， 轉向無線通訊規格升級與連網終端數量擴張 。 其中 ，
WiFi 7為目前最明確的新增需求來源，除手機、PC及Router持續升級外，
應用範圍亦逐步延伸至AI眼鏡 、 無人機 、 機器人 、 智慧家庭及其他IoT設備 。
隨終端裝置導入更高速、更低延遲的無線連接規格，對PA輸出功率、線性
度與效率的要求同步提升，使 GaAs需求不再僅與智慧型手機銷售高度連
動，而是逐步擴展至更廣泛的連網設備市場。

全新為全球 最大砷化鎵磊晶廠 ，
近期受光通訊需求增加，光電子
產品占比逐步提升。

手機終端需求成長放緩，然規格
升級及終端應用增加，帶動 GaAs
需求提升。

### Page 3

請參見末頁重要披露及免責聲明 3

下一世代WiFi 8則有望延續此一規格升級趨勢。相較過去WiFi世代主要追
求傳輸速度提升，WiFi 8進一步強調低延遲、穩定連線、長距離覆蓋與更
高上行流量(uplink)效能，應用場景也更貼近AI Edge Device、機器人及
即時互聯設備。整體而言，GaAs微電子產業的成長邏輯由手機出貨成長轉
向單機RF價值提升及連網裝置數量增加。

(2)  AI光互連升級推升InP需求，成為Ⅲ-V族主要成長動能 
生成式AI帶動CSP持續擴大資料中心投資，隨GPU與ASIC叢集規模增加，光
模組規格由400G快速升級至800G、1.6T，並朝3.2T發展，使高速PD、EML及
CW Laser 需 求 同 步 提 升 。LightCounting 於2026/7 最 新 預 估 ，2026 年
Ethernet光收發模組銷售額將年增73%，並預估2031年市場規模達800億美
元，反映AI高速光互連需求仍處於快速成長階段。

隨單通道速率由100G提升至200G， 接收端PD對頻寬要求提高 ， 發射端Laser
亦朝更高功率與高速率升級，使InP成為高速光通訊的關鍵材料。另一方
面，SiPh滲透率提升並不會取代InP， 因矽本身無法有效發光 ， 仍須搭配InP 
CW Laser 作為光源；後續 NPO/CPO 導 入 亦 將 延 續 外置 光 源 需 求 。同時
LightCounting指出在近期需求再度上修後，原先預期緩解的InP Laser短
缺可能延續至2027年中，顯示InP需求增速仍高於供給擴張。

(3) 上游原料高度集中中國，地緣政治加劇Ⅲ-V族供給限制 
Ⅲ-V族上游原料供給高度集中於中國，其中全球約98%的Gallium產量來自
中國 ，InP所需Indium亦約70%由中國供應 ， 使GaAs與InP供應鏈對中國政策
高度敏感 。 隨中美科技競爭升溫 ， 中國自2023年起對Gallium及相關化合物
實施出口許可，2025年再將InP基板納入出口管制，目前GaAs、Ge及InP基
板出口均須取得中國商務部許可，部分產品供貨時程已受到審批進度影
響。因此，原料供應高度集中與出口管制已成為影響Ⅲ-V族材料供應穩定
性及出貨時程的重要變數。

營運回顧及展望分析 
1. 2Q26 本業穩健改善，匯損低基期推升獲利大幅成長 
全新2Q26營收達9.65億元(+0.6%QoQ，+35.2%YoY)， 創單季歷史新高 ， 主要
受惠AI資料中心相關光電子需求持續成長，以及 Wi-Fi等微電子需求維持
穩健。毛利率為38.61%(+0.5ppts QoQ，+4.2ppts YoY)，主要受惠產品漲
價轉嫁基板及原物料成本，加上高毛利光電子產品占比提升。營業費用達
1.49億元(+7.3%QoQ，+20.6%YoY)、業外利益達0.13億元 ， 較去年同期業外
損失0.98億元大幅改善(2Q25受到新台幣急升造成匯兌損失)，使2Q26稅後
淨 利 達2.14 億元(+9.5%QoQ ，+488.3%YoY) ，EPS 為1.15 元(+8.5%QoQ ，
+475%YoY)。2Q26產品組合方面：微電子73%、光電子27%；相較1Q26微電子
75%、光電子25%，光電子營收占比持續提升。

光互連高速成長，接收發射端皆
需要 InP 關鍵材料。

率季增年增。

2. 基板到位推升光電子放量，3Q26 營收獲利可望再創高 
全新 7 月 自 結 ， 營 收 達4.22 億元 (+45.11%YoY) 、 稅 後 淨 利1.15 億元
(+236.97%YoY)、EPS為0.62元 。 研究部以過往匯兌損益以及費用率去預估 ，
毛利率約為42%， 優於2Q26的38.6%， 受惠高毛利光電子產品比重提升 。8月
營收達4.71億元(+11.6%MoM，+71.2%YoY)， 累計3Q26達成率為67%， 符合研
究 部 預 期 。 產 品 組 合 方 面 ， 微 電 子 53.9%(-6ppts MoM) ，光電子
46.1%(+6ppts MoM)，光電子佔比提升受惠InP基板出口許可陸續取得、基
板供應改善 ， 以及客戶自帶基板增加 ； 然微電子進入3Q傳統手機新品旺季 ，
亦使營收穩健成長。研究部預期在光通訊需求高速成長下，預期4Q26有機
會超越微電子產品形成交叉，進而帶動整體毛利率。研究部預估3Q26營收
為13.92億元，EPS為1.69元。

3. 200G PD 1Q27 放量，CW Laser、EML 接續推升發射端成長  
接收端方面，目前新增PD專案以200G為主，美系大客戶已進入量產。目前
200G PD 占比仍低，但美系客戶客供料已陸續進廠，預計1Q27開始明顯放
量，屆時200G PD有機會占整體PD營收50%以上。200G PD技術門檻及ASP均
明顯優於100G，因此除帶動營收成長外，產品組合亦將持續往高階移動。
發射端方面，CW Laser目前已進入量產並開始出貨，2026年仍以小量出貨
為主 ， 預計2027年隨既有客戶需求提升進一步放量 。 此外 ， 目前已有陸系 、
台系及日系等多家客戶合作 ， 公司亦正與美系大客戶洽談新案 ；EML目前在
客戶驗證階段，預計於1H27開始放量，將成為發射端新增營收來源。管理
層預期2027年隨1.6T需求成長、CW Laser 及EML出貨規模擴大，以及發射
端ASP相較接收端1.5倍以上，發射端營收有望超越接收端，成為光電子下
一階段主要成長來源。

4. 既有產能彈性轉向 InP，新增機台支撐 2027 光電子成長 
全新目前共有67台MOCVD，其中64台可於GaAs及InP間彈性共用、3台為GaN
專用設備 。7月營收雖創歷史新高 ， 但產能利用率仍僅50%以上，顯示MOCVD
設備本身具有餘裕， 現階段限制光電子出貨的主要因素仍為 InP基板供應
限制。 由於GaAs與InP共用機台轉換僅需3–5天 ， 若2027年基板供應持續改
善，公司可依訂單需求及產品毛利率，逐步將部分低毛利微電子產能轉向
PD、CW Laser、EML等高毛利InP光電子產品。近期，公司因應需求再新增
2台MOCVD供InP產能使用 ， 預計3Q27到廠 ， 屆時總機台數將由67台提升至69
台。

需求端方面，Lumentum持續擴充產能，但供給仍然落後客戶需求，供需缺
口由原先的25-30%擴大至30%以上。因此研究部認為，在磷化銦基板供應逐
步改善以及供需吃緊下，全新有望將既有GaAs/InP共用機台產能轉換，逐
步轉向高單價、高毛利光電子產品。綜上所述，研究部保守假設2027年部
分GaAs產能轉為InP使用 ， 搭配新增2台InP設備貢獻 ， 預估2027年光電子營
收年增138%。

投資建議 
產能不是問題，基板供應改善推升營收獲利成長

研究部初次給予全新買進建議 ， 主因為 ：(1)InP 基板供應改善帶動光電子
快速放量 ， 且高毛利光電子占比由1H26 約26%提升至7 月40%、8 月46.1%，
光電子超越微電子的黃金交叉將近 ；(2)產品組合轉佳 、較高毛利的客供料
占比逐步提升及價格調整效益帶動獲利改善，管理層預期 3Q26 毛利率可
回升至 40%以上；(3)展望 2027 年，美系客戶200G PD 預計 1Q27 開始明顯
放量，CW Laser 及 EML 發射端則接續放量，管理層預期 2027 年發射端營
收 有 望 超 越 接 收 端 。 綜 上 所 述 ， 研 究 部 預 估 全 新2026/2027 營收為
49.02/78.77 億元，分別年增 45%/60.7%，EPS 分別為 6.08/11.63 元，評

營收獲利成長，因此給予 60 倍本益比，目標價 700 元(60PER*2027EPS)。

## Document 070: 260910_gs_TSMC

Source PDF: all report pdf/260910_gs_TSMC.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-10
Pages: 10
Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

Presenters: Wendell Huang, SVP & CFO  
Bottom Line: We have three key takeaways: (1) TSMC continues to view AI as a 
multi-year megatrend that remains at a very early stage, with lower compute costs 
expected to accelerate AI adoption and ultimately drive greater demand for 
advanced silicon; (2) execution in Arizona continues to progress well, with Phase 1 
achieving yields comparable to Taiwan and already generating profits, while TSMC 
expects approximately 30% of its N2-and-beyond capacity to be located outside 
Taiwan in five years, primarily in Arizona; and (3) despite dilution from the N2 ramp 
and overseas expansion, management remains comfortable achieving its long-term 
gross margin target of 56% and above, supported by disciplined capacity planning, 
high utilization, productivity improvements, cost reductions, and pricing that reflects 
TSMC’s value. 
Key Takeaways

AI remains in the early stages of a multi-year megatrend: TSMC continues to n
see increasing adoption of AI. Management also highlighted the shift from 
generative AI toward agentic AI, which should broaden compute demand 
beyond accelerators to CPUs. TSMC remains confident in the durability of the AI 
cycle based on discussions not only with its direct customers but also with its 
customers’ customers. Recent visits of US CSPs further reinforced management’s 
confidence, as cloud service providers appeared well prepared in areas including 
power and broader infrastructure deployment. 
Lower compute costs should drive greater consumption and silicon demand: n
Management believes open-source models and continued improvements in 
computing efficiency will reduce token costs, leading to greater AI 
consumption and broader adoption, supporting incremental demand for 
advanced silicon. TSMC has already incorporated this dynamic into its capacity 
planning and continues to expand aggressively to support what it views as

### Page 2

structural, multi-year demand growth.
Disciplined demand validation remains critical amid aggressive expansion: n
TSMC uses a combination of top-down and bottom-up analysis to validate demand.
Its top-down assessment considers macroeconomic conditions, semiconductor
demand, fabless/system companies, the foundry industry, etc, while its bottom-up
approach evaluates demand across different segments and incorporates feedback
from customers and customers’ customers. Management acknowledged that

semiconductors will remain cyclical, but believes correctly identifying the underlying
megatrend is more important than attempting to forecast every short-term
fluctuation.
Arizona execution is demonstrating that TSMC’s manufacturing model can n
travel: TSMC reiterated that overseas expansion is based on customer demand for
geographic flexibility and an appropriate level of government support. Arizona
Phase 1, using N4 technology, is in operation, with yields comparable to Taiwan,

satisfactory quality and reliability, and positive profitability. Management views
this as an important milestone because it demonstrates internally and to customers
that TSMC can produce wafers in the US with the same quality as in Taiwan.
Equipment move-in for Phase 2, which will use N3 technology, is expected to begin
soon; construction of Phase 3 has started; and preparation work for Phase 4 and the
first US advanced-packaging facility is underway.

Arizona has substantial room for further expansion: In addition to its original n
Arizona development, TSMC has acquired another parcel of land capable of
accommodating an additional five to six fabs, supporting its recently
announced incremental US$100bn investment. Based on its current plan, TSMC
expects approximately 30% of its N2-and-beyond capacity to be located outside
Taiwan in five years, primarily in Arizona. However, the most advanced technologies

will continue to ramp first in Taiwan because the early-stage technology transfer
requires close collaboration and frequent movement of engineers among R&D and
manufacturing sites. Overseas deployment will generally follow after the technology
has stabilized in Taiwan.
Customers increasingly value and are willing to pay for geographic flexibility: n
Management noted that customers initially requested only a modest amount of
geographically diversified supply, but their requirements have increased as TSMC has

demonstrated successful execution in Arizona. TSMC believes this geographic
flexibility represents incremental value and intends to reflect that value in its pricing,
with customers increasingly willing to recognize the associated premium.
Technology, manufacturing excellence, capacity, and trust underpin TSMC’s n
competitive moat: Management believes customers select a foundry partner based
on access to the best technology, the ability to ramp rapidly into high-volume

manufacturing with attractive economics, sufficient capacity, and confidence that
the foundry will not compete with its customers. TSMC is confident in maintaining
this lead by continuing to advance its roadmap. Management also highlighted its
record of rapidly ramping new technologies, the scale of its wafer and
advanced-packaging investments, and its consistent delivery against customer

### Page 3

commitments as key elements of customer trust that cannot be replicated through
CapEx or engineering recruitment alone.
Pricing remains strategic rather than opportunistic: TSMC does not intend to raise n
prices simply because near-term utilization is high, nor reduce prices simply because
utilization temporarily weakens. Instead, the company’s approach is to price
sustainably and consistently based on the value it provides, while ensuring that
customers can remain successful over the long term. Management noted that

TSMC’s structural profitability has continued to improve, with its long-term gross
margin target increasing from 50% five years ago to 53% and now 56% and above.
Leading-edge wafer and advanced-packaging capacity remain tight: n
Management continues to build capacity wherever possible to meet customer
demand. N3 demand remains particularly strong: unlike prior technology cycles,
when demand for a node typically began declining two to three years after its

introduction, TSMC is adding further N3 capacity and still does not expect supply
to be sufficient. The company is also expanding advanced-packaging capacity to
address strong accelerator demand. Outside TSMC, management identified power
and memory as potential bottlenecks cited by other parts of the AI supply chain,
while emphasizing that foundry capacity itself remains difficult to expand because
fabs require two to three years to build and another one to two years to ramp.

TSMC’s disclosed AI revenue understates its broader exposure: Management n
reiterated that its disclosed AI revenue definition is relatively narrow and primarily
captures GPUs, custom AI accelerators and memory base die. It excludes CPUs and
networking products because TSMC cannot reliably determine whether each chip is
ultimately deployed in an AI system. As agentic AI drives incremental demand across
x86, Arm, and RISC-V CPUs, as well as networking and other supporting silicon,

TSMC’s total AI-related exposure is therefore broader than its reported
AI-accelerator revenue. The company intends to retain its existing definition until it
can more accurately distinguish the end use of these products.
No visible barrier to continued transistor scaling: TSMC is currently ramping N2, n
with A14 expected approximately two years later, while development of the
subsequent node is already underway. Management does not currently see a

technical issue preventing delivery of the next node or continued advancement
beyond the existing roadmap. TSMC views close collaboration with customers as a
key foundry advantage, allowing the company to develop each technology against
specific customer performance, power, density, and economic requirements.
Cross-node capacity optimization is an underappreciated advantage: TSMC n
highlighted its ability to generate additional output through productivity

improvements and to convert tools and capacity across technology nodes. For
example, the company can use portions of its N5 capacity to support N3 demand
and can also optimize capacity across less-adjacent nodes where technically
feasible. Management views this cross-node flexibility as a distinctive element of
TSMC’s manufacturing excellence, allowing the company to respond more
quickly to demand changes while reducing the risk of capacity obsolescence.

Advanced packaging is strategic primarily because it enables wafer growth: n
10 September 2026   3
Goldman Sachs TSMC (2330.TW)For the exclusive use of KEVINLU@LENOVO.COM
e92c7a75ab8b4efbba794e6b187208c8

### Page 4

CoWoS capacity remains tight, and TSMC already started outsourcing selected 
packaging processes to OSAT partners to support additional growth. Management 
emphasized that advanced packaging is intended primarily to ensure and enable 
wafer demand rather than serve as a standalone profit pool. TSMC is therefore 
developing multiple packaging architectures, including panel-level packaging, etc, 
while remaining open to customers using alternative packaging providers, as either 
approach ultimately supports demand for TSMC wafers. 
Advanced-packaging execution remains a key differentiator: TSMC noted that its n
current advanced-packaging capability supports approximately 5.5x reticle size, 
with a roadmap to reach approximately 14x reticle sizes within the next several 
years. While competing roadmaps may also appear attractive, management believes 
execution and the ability to deliver in high-volume manufacturing will ultimately 
determine competitive outcomes. TSMC does not believe competitors can use 
advanced-packaging wins to meaningfully displace its leading-edge wafer 
business, as foundry and packaging remain fundamentally different businesses. 
A unified TSMC culture supports overseas manufacturing execution: TSMC’s n
objective is not to create separate Taiwan and US cultures, but to establish a 
consistent TSMC culture centered on integrity, commitment, innovation, and 
customer trust (ICIC). Locally hired Arizona employees spend six to eighteen months 
training and working in Taiwan, while experienced Taiwan-based employees are 
assigned to Arizona to work alongside local teams. Over time, the number of Taiwan 
assignees should decline as locally trained employees assume greater responsibility. 
TSMC is applying this approach across its overseas manufacturing sites. 
Management remains comfortable with its 56%-and-above long-term gross n
margin target: TSMC reiterated its 6 major drivers of profitability: new-technology 
ramp, pricing, cost, product mix, utilization, and FX. The N2 ramp is expected to 
dilute 2026 GM by approximately 2-3ppts, but its profitability should improve over 
time toward the corporate average; management also noted that N2’s structural 
profitability is better than N3 at a comparable stage. Overseas expansion is 
expected to dilute GM by 2-3ppts during the early portion of the current five-year 
period, then widening to 3-ppts later as more overseas fabs begin production. Each 
new fab will initially create dilution before improving along its learning curve. Taking 
these puts and takes together, management remains very comfortable that 
disciplined capacity planning, healthy utilization, cost reduction, productivity 
gains, and pricing that reflects TSMC’s value will enable the company to deliver 
for shareholders and achieve its long-term gross margin target ‘of 56% and 
higher’ with focus on the ‘higher’ side. 
Valuation/Risks

TSMC (Buy): Our 12-month price target is NT$3,100, which is derived by applying a 
target P/E multiple of 22x to our 2027E EPS. Our 22x target P/E is benchmarked against 
1.0stdv above its 5-year trading average. For the ADR (TSM), we have a 12-month price 
target of US$620, based on a USD/TWD rate of 30.0 and an ADR premium of 20%. Key

We expect Luxshare, Lingyi, Crystal, and AAC to be the key
beneficiaries of the new iPhone launch. We downgrade Largan
to EW and Genius to UW.  Both can benefit from the variable
aperture lens upgrade, but enthusiasm over Co-Packaged Optics

has made the stocks overvalued.
The iPhone opportunity is real for Largan and Genius…but their stocks have
rallied 48% and 85%, respectively, in the past month: (The TAIEX is up 5% over
this period.)
We now value Largan at NT$7,100/share – no longer attractive: Our analysis
suggests that Largan's current share price already embeds more than 30% global
market share in Fiber Array Units (FAU) before formal production starts in 2H27 or
even 2028. Our residual income model yields a value of NT$3,000/share for the

company's traditional business, while our TAM analysis derives a value of NT$4,100/
share for CPO/FAU new business, bringing the total price target to NT$7,100.
However, any delay in CPO/FAU development poses significant downside risk. We
therefore downgrade to EW.
We now value Genius at NT$910/share – but  even on this basis, we view it as
overvalued: Similarly, we believe Genius's share price is also inflated by hopes for
FAU components. Using a similar approach, we conclude that aggregate value is NT

$910/share (NT$600 for existing business and NT$310/share for FAU component
business). We recommend taking profits.
Reiterate OW on Luxshare, Lingyi, Crystal and AAC: We believe all four companies
will benefit from the new iPhone launch. Here, however,  we still see upside in the
stocks. We see these companies, benefiting in various ways:
• Luxshare: Key player in iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max assembly, also benefits from
variable aperture upgrade as component supplier.

•  Lingyi: Higher content value form both iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and foldable.
•  Crystal: Micro prism modules, coated filters, and cover lenses should enjoy
positive ASP and volume growth.
• AAC: Vapor chamber (VC) heat dissipation upgrade for iPhone 18 Pro Max
and Pro is the key catalyst.
Remain EW on Sunny Optical and GoerTek: Sunny is a key variable aperture
component vendor, but it's been well on track to meet the goal of doubling revenue,
implying limited upside surprise. GoerTek could face labor shortages and margin

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.

Executive Summary
With Largan and Genius's significant outperformance YTD, we believe the iPhone 18
launch is less likely to become a key driver of further stock price movement for them.
Instead, our analysis suggests that the CPO enthusiasm could have already made these
stocks overvalued. We therefore downgrade Largan from OW to  EW and downgrade
Genius from EW  to UW.
Meanwhile, we expect Luxshare, Lingyi, Crystal, and AAC to become the key beneficiaries

amid iPhone new product launches. These stocks haven't rallied materially, and we see
upside potential in them.
We maintain EW ratings on Sunny and GoerTek and expect limited positive surprise from
the iPhone peak season.

Morgan Stanley Research 5
Implications from iPhone 18 Launch for Various Supply
Chain Companies
Camera spec upgrade is a positive earnings driver, but CPO
enthusiasm has made Largan and Genius overvalued
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have applied a variable aperture main camera for the first
time, representing a significant hardware upgrade.  The ASP of  variable aperture lenses will
be higher than it is for traditional lenses. Thus, a rapid shipment increase in 3Q26 could

become a key re-rating catalyst – indeed, it has already prompted sharp re-rating for
Largan, Genius, and Sunny.
Besides this, the launch of Apple's first foldable iPhone will also provide an incremental
demand driver beyond the standard iPhone 18 lineup. According to Nikkei Asia (link),
foldable smartphone orders increased from 8 million units to 10 million units this year,
and if the new product performs well in 4Q2026, it could become a positive catalyst for

Apple supply chain companies.
Beyond variable aperture and foldable, the further development of a new periscope lens
with the key customer is likely to expand  these use of periscope lenses in the future. This
could also become a positive driver for optical lens companies in the supply chain.
1. Largan: iPhone opportunity is real, but recent enthusiasm
over CPO made valuation too aggressive – downgrade to EW
Largan's revenue follows a well-established seasonal pattern tied to Apple's annual iPhone

launch cycle. After shipments declined continuously from March 2026 through June 2026,
we expect a seasonal recovery to begin in 3Q26, with sequential increases highly likely in
the following months. Largan's August 2026 consolidated revenue reached NT$5.012
billion, up 3% month-over-month and its best performance in four months, and the
company expects September's shipment momentum to surpass August's.
Largan is a key supplier of variable aperture lenses for the iPhone 18 Pro series, and the

company could also benefit from foldable and periscope opportunities, we raise our
intrinsic value estimate of the company's traditional business from NT$2,814/share to NT
$3,000/share. For more details, please refer to Exhibit 18.
Besides the Apple lens opportunity, we believe Largan's share performance is also highly
correlated to CPO development. In order to assess the fundamental value from the CPO
opportunity, we undertook the following analysis:

1. We forecast CPO optical engine volume to increase from 0.39mn in 2026 to
7.78mn in 2027,with a further surge to 48.6mn in 2028. Consequently, FAU (Fiber
Array Units – vital optical interconnect components that align multiple optical
fibers with silicon chips, making them critical for Co-Packaged Optics) volume for
CPO also grows from 0.39 to 48.6 mn for the same period of time;
2. We assume ASP of US$100 in 2026-2028 (average market level);
3. We forecast Largan's FAU market share to increase from 0% in 2026 to 5% in

4. Assuming net margins of 10% in 2027 and 30% in 2028, we forecast FAU earnings

4. Crystal: Prisms, coated filters, and cover lenses to benefit
We expect Crystal Optech to benefit from Apple's new product launch because  the
company is supplying three key products in the supply chain:
1. Its micro prism modules are a key enabling component for periscope (folded-

optics) telephoto cameras in smartphones. The company's prism technology uses a
folded optical path to achieve long-focal-length telephoto capability without
increasing device thickness. In 1H26, the micro prism module business enjoyed
significant volume growth. The iPhone 18 launch will directly extend this demand
into 2H26.
2. Crystal-Optech's coated filter business — which brings micro-nano optical
processing into the IRCF manufacturing process to significantly improve petal

ghosting and chromatic aberration in special imaging scenarios — is another key
segment that benefits from the iPhone 18 launch. Apple's high-end Pro models are
the primary application for this product, so the company is highly likely to
generate rapid revenue and earnings growth.
3. The iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to feature advances in 3D sensing,
including a smaller Dynamic Island as some Face ID components move beneath the
display, which sustains demand for these optical components. Crystal Optech is

well positioned to capture the growth opportunity in iPhone's 3D sensing and
cover lenses.
The company's 2Q26 results were a bit weaker than we expected because of rising costs
from R&D and capacity expansion related to new products. However, we believe this
investment could lead to stronger growth in 2028 and onward. As a result, we trim our
earnings estimates 15.6% for 2026 and 2.9% for 2027 but raise our 2028 estimate 8.2%.
Consequently, we raise our price target  7%, to Rmb32, implying 24% upside from the

current level.

We expect Luxshare to benefit from the latest new product  launch through the following

four key drivers:
1.  Second largest assembler for iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max — the most premium-heavy
iPhone lineup in history. If the  Pro/Pro Max models can take 70%+ of total iPhone
volume, it could mark the highest high-end model contribution over the past
several model cycles. A higher share from high-end models implies better revenue
and margin outlook for Luxshare.
2.   Capturing component opportunity in new  variable aperture actuator supply.

Instead of doing assembly, Lxushare is also playing the role  of supplier of actuator
mechanisms for the variable aperture camera system in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro
Max. This helps Luxshare gain exposure to high-end component business, which
carries higher margin than assembly business.
3. Foldable iPhone (iPhone Ultra) exposure: While Luxshare is not the assembler for
the foldable phone, it has actively developed foldable hinge technology, with R&D

focused on high-precision, long-life, large-angle hinge modules for inward-folding

4.  Leading AirPods assembly share:  In the AirPods assembly market, we expect

Despite a significant FX loss, Luxshare posted resilient earnings in 1H26. We nudge our

AAC: Key beneficiary of  iPhone VC application
AAC Tech is one of Apple's key component suppliers, providing a broad portfolio spanning
acoustics, haptics, and thermal management. The iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and iPhone Ultra
launch is a direct, multi-dimensional catalyst across all those business segments.
Within the three segments, we believe thermal management –  Vapor Chamber (VC) Heat
Dissipation – is the most important catalyst. AAC Technologies is a key vendor of VC heat

spreaders in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The significant expansion of the VC cooling
area is driven by the iPhone 18 Pro's A20 Pro chip, which debuts on a 2nm process node
with complex WMCM packaging technology to support on-device AI computation, leading
to increased thermal output. Apple first introduced VC liquid cooling in the iPhone 17 Pro
series, with AAC as the primary supplier for that generation as well.
This division has already demonstrated significant growth momentum heading into the

iPhone 18 ramp up. In 1H26, heat dissipation revenue surged approximately 400% YoY, to
RMB1.10 billion, primarily driven by the continued ramp-up in shipments of high-
performance innovative vapor chambers. The company expects VC shipments to exceed
180,000k units in 2026, up from 140,000k+  units in 2025.

While Apple is BYDE's key customer, accounting for >50% of total revenue, it is mainly
from the  iPad assembly business. Therefore, this division is less likely to benefit from the
iPhone 18 launch.
The company is also the second-largest iPhone metal casing vendor, supplying precision
structural components including titanium and aluminium alloy chassis. While iPhone 18
launch is the direct driver for this segment, the titanium-to-aluminium downgrade has

become a near-term headwind.  Titanium is a higher-value, higher-margin material for BYDE

Despite the lackluster outlook, we expect earnings to show sequential improvement in
3Q26, driven by the normal peak season in 3Q26, followed by stronger growth in 4Q26 as
liquid cooling products for AI infrastructure also ramp up. Our earnings estimates and

price target remain unchanged.
GoerTek: Margin might face pressures despite peak season
GoerTek's primary Apple exposure is in smart acoustic complete units (AirPods assembly
and components) and precision components. We believe the  iPhone 18 launch and peak
season ramp in 3Q–4Q will drive higher shipment volumes for these products.
However, GoerTek's transfer of production  to Vietnam — where it has invested
approximately US$1.3 billion through multiple entities — has created a persistent labor

cost headwind. In 2H25, a labor shortage caused by the rapid capacity transfer forced
GoerTek to offer higher wages, triggering material  gross margin pressure  for the smart
acoustic assembly business. Overall gross margins partially recovered to 13.8% in 1Q26
and 15.2% in 2Q26, but the underlying trend of rising wages in Vietnam remains a
structural factor. As GoerTek ramps production for the iPhone 18 peak season in 3Q and
4Q, the higher labor cost base in Vietnam will continue to weigh on assembly margins.

We raise our 2026 and 2027 earnings estimates 14.9% and 10.6%, respectively, mainly
reflecting the better-than-expected gross margin recovery in 1H26. However, we raise our
price target only modestly: 4%. to Rmb27, as persistent labor-cost pressure in Vietnam
could limit further margin expansion and reduce the earnings benefit from higher peak-
season volumes.
Considering the factors discussed above, we believe GoerTek is less likely to benefit from

the new iPhone product launch and peak season volume increase.

Where we could be wrong
While we expect iPhone 18 to be  a positive catalyst in 2H26, we are watching three key
variables on the potential inflection points:
1.  Memory prices: These are a key variable this year. If there is a memory price
correction anytime during 2026, investors are likely to expect an earlier
smartphone shipment and margin recovery, which could reverse the negative

sentiment.
2.  LLMs: We see LLMs as a revolutionary innovation. They could introduce numerous
creative features in smartphone applications and change user habits in the years to
come. If the Edge AI breakthrough arrives earlier than we expect, it could
accelerate the smartphone product cycle and make the recovery earlier.
3. iPhone sales performance: Better-than-expected sell-through of the iPhone 18
Pro, Pro Max and its first foldable model could drive shipment upside, higher

content value and stronger capacity utilization. Conversely, weaker demand could
lead to order cuts after the initial ramp up and reduce the earnings benefits from
key hardware upgrades.

We hosted TECO (1504.TW, not covered) management at our Asia Leaders 
Conference 2026 (Aug 31 - Sep 2) in Hong Kong. Management is positive on their 
data center business, which includes construction services, products (e.g. 
transformer, busway, AC motor controls, etc.), and modular data center (MDC). 
Management remains positive on data center demand in Southeast Asia, highlighting 
a major CSP client’s 1GW (5-year) plan in Thailand, Malaysia, and potential in 
Indonesia in the future. The positive tone echoes our positive view on the AI 
infrastructure cycle, on which we raised our AI servers implied AI chips forecast by 
14% / 22% / 14% in 2026E-28E in June (report link) to +75% / 42% / 20% YoY in 
2026E-28E, or 19m / 27m / 32m in 2026E-28E. Capex estimates on leading US CSPs 
was also raised by 8% / 27% / 25% in 2026E-28E to +76% / +35% / +8% YoY in 
2026E-28E, or up to US$1.1tn by 2028E (report link). As we highlighted in our FII 
Chairman and Innolight Chairman visits takeaways, supply chain remains positive on 
rising AI investments in coming years, with spending across CSP , NeoCloud, 
Government, and Enterprise, and we are at an early stage of infrastructure spending 
and application development. End-customers are involved more in supply chain 
product development and capacity investment, also better reflecting real demand.  
Company profile: TECO (1504.TW, not covered) was founded in 1956, starting with 
motor manufacturing and is currently among the five largest industrial motor 
suppliers worldwide. The company mainly offers electromechanical systems, with 
three major business groups of Green Mechatronic Solutions, Intelligence Energy, 
and Air & Intelligent Life. Apart from its traditional motor business, TECO is 
expanding in new markets including ESCO low-carbon solutions, EV powertrain, 
offshore wind power, energy storage system and data center engineering. The 
company has built 700 MV of data centers in Southeast Asia. 
Key Takeaways

1. Data center business: Management remains positive on the business and stated 
they provide both construction services across power, cooling, and networking, and

### Page 2

related products (e.g. transformer, busway, AC motor controls, etc.). The company’s data
center business focuses on Southeast Asia, where a major customer (a leading US CSP)
announced a 1GW data center in Malaysia (announced in 2025), 1GW data center in
Thailand (announced in 2026), and potential new data center in Indonesia. Other than
leading US CSPs, the company also sees opportunities in sovereign AI, for example,
Japan is planning a 5-year 350mW AI data center, which could use MDC (modular data

center) for speedy deployment.
2. Modular Data Center (MDC) strength: Management highlights MDC saves AI data
center deployment time by ~50% to within 9 months, and reducing 15-20% capex, as it
moves most work into factory production, reducing onsite engineering. Modular Data
Center includes: modular IT server system, modular UPS system, modular power
distribution system, modular container genset system (power generation), and modular
cooling system, facilitating the AI data center deployment. The company’s product in

Malaysia is also for a leading US CSP , which one MDC could deliver 2.7mW.

Industry View In-Line
Overall August ODM notebook shipments came in 19% below our estimate: Pull-
forward demand appears to have come to an end, channel partners and distributors
have stocked up on inventory, and OEMs are slowing their sales into the channel.
We believe this is the main reason why August NB builds came in slower than our

expectation. However, we continue to expect product mix to continue to shift
toward higher-end, more-profitable models. Several ODMs such as Quanta and
Compal have even lowered 3Q NB build forecasts compared to their earlier guidance
on 2Q earnings calls three weeks ago. Thus we lower our 3Q NB build estimate by
7% to 25.4M units (-16% q/q, -25% y/y). This sequential decline is sub-seasonal vs.
the 15-year average seasonality of +5% q/q in 3Q, and implies September NB builds

at 9.9M units (+35% m/m, -18% y/y).
We introduce our 4Q notebook build estimate at 23.9M units (-6% q/q, -26% y/
y): This sequential decline is sub-seasonal (despite an already lowered base in 3Q)
vs. the 15-year average seasonality of flat q/q in 4Q. None of the ODMs have
provided official guidance for 4Q notebook builds, but our preliminary checks
suggests that they will continue to fall q/q. On our estimate, this implies that the
top 5 Taiwan NB ODMs' builds for CY26 will come in at ~108.8M units (-16% y/

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
Top five ODMs' August 2026 NB shipments were 7.3M units (-11% m/m, -35% y/y),
19% below our estimate.
We see September 2026 NB builds at 9.9M units (+35% m/m, -18% y/y).
We lower our 3Q26 NB build estimate by 7% to 25.4M units (-16% q/q, -25% y/y).
We introduce our 4Q26 NB build estimate at 23.9M units (-6% q/q, -26% y/y).

Our top five ODMs' CY26 NB build estimate is ~108.8M units (-16% y/y).

### Page 1

ab 14 September 2026
Global Research
First Read
Parade Technologies
2026 Taiwan Summit: Near-term outlook
impacted by softer NB demand
Q326 revenue tracking toward lower-end of guidance
Parade attended our 2026 Taiwan Summit on Sep 14th. August sales of NT$1,327 mn
was down 2% and flat YoY. QTD sales only reached 57% of UBSe and Street estimates,
and Parade now expects its Q326 sales could come in at the lower-end of its US$139–
153 mn guidance range, likely due to softer NB demand. Parade's GM declined by 0.1

pp QoQ to 40.2% in Q226 on OSAT price hike, as the Taiwanese OSATs have allocated
more capacity to AI-related products. Parade noted it has been adding new OSAT
partners in Korea, China, and Malaysia, while also adjusting its ASPs in Q326. It noted its
Q326F GM should come in within its 40-44% guidance range, but we believe the GM
expansion will be more moderate given the cost headwinds. Q326F OPEX guidance is
reiterated at US$33-36 mn with full year OPEX growth to be within 5% YoY, and

effective tax rate for 2026F is guided to remain slightly above 10%. It has not provided a
specific outlook for Q426 but acknowledge the challenging outlook for the laptop
market. This is consistent with our recent checks within the NB display supply chain.
ASIC for CPU chipset to tape out soon for H227 mass production
Parade highlighted its deep expertise in high-speed connectivity and proprietary IP,
which enables it to deliver customized ASIC-like solutions to its customers. While its

initial focus was  display applications, it is now expanding  into CPU chipset. It is on-track
to tape out two chipsets for its CPU  customer, targeting  different PCIe channel
configurations. Comparing with its peers solution on 28nm node, Parade believes its
product  developed on 12 nm node  offers superior power efficiency. Parade noted the
CPU chipsets are  on track for mass production by H227, although we believe ASMedia's
solution will start to ramp from mid-2027 and will split the market share with Parade.

Exploring additional growth drivers for 2027
Parade also highlighted its ongoing effort to diversify away from traditional NB display  IC
business with several initiatives expected to contribute growth from 2027F. It sees good
revenue opportunity for  integrated touch solutions (TED/TTED), especially after the
potential adoption of touch display by  its standard-plus customer. For ACC cables, it will
supply redriver  with switch function, which should be a new growth engine in 2027F as

it believes copper and optical will co-exist in the next several years. Its USB4 retimer also
has good market share at non-Intel platform and management expects the penetration
to exceed  50% in 2027 vs 40%+ in 2026. Parade also noted its automotive business
should see strong sales growth in 2027, although we estimate overall contribution for
this segment remains at low-single-digit  % of total revenue.
Valuation: Rate NEUTRAL with NT$610 PT
We have a NEUTRAL rating on Parade with NT$610 PT,  based on 14.5x forward PE.

Company Description
Founded in 2005, Parade is a mixed-signal IC fabless design house headquartered in San Jose,
CA, specialising in high-speed interface and display solutions used in PCs, servers, consumer
electronics and display panels. Parade's display solutions (55% of 2024 revenue) include

embedded display port timing controllers (eDP TCON), source drivers and touch controllers.
Parade's high-speed interface solutions (45% of 2025 revenue) include signal conditioners
for USB, PCIe, SATA, etc, as well as protocol converters and USB controllers.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
Our price target for Parade is based on target PE multiple.
Fabless integrated circuit (IC) design houses face a variety of uncertainties, including rapidly

changing technology, end-market demand, competition, employee turnover and foundry
wafer costs. They are also vulnerable to legal disputes over IP rights.
For Parade, we believe key risks include: 1) Demand dynamics in PCs/notebooks, TVs, servers,
etc., as any pickup or slowdown in these end-markets would directly impact Parade's growth
and new product rollouts. 2) The length of the qualification cycle or pace of adoption by
clients could be a key upside/downside risk to our thesis. 3) Potential new entrants in Apple's

IT display timing controllers could be a downside risk to our growth estimates. 4) Fiercer price
competition by global and Asian peers may pose downside risk to our growth and GM
forecasts. 5) Foundry and assembly cost changes could present upside/downside risks to our
GM estimates.

Investing in structured investments involves significant risks. For a detailed discussion of the risks involved in investing in any particular structured investment, you must read

the relevant offering materials for that investment. Structured investments are unsecured obligations of a particular issuer with returns linked to the performance of an
underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

before investing in any securities.

16 September 2026
Global Research
First Read
BizLink Holding
UBS T aiwan Summit 2026 key takeaways:
margins improve as HPC sales build
Positive outlook amid market volatilities
Bizlink's share price has been volatile amid gross margin weakness in Q126 and a
conservative read-through from Credo's earnings call on AEC products. Bizlink's
management remains positive about  its order momentum in HPC products, with data
cable shipments picking up, and power cable shipments  growing alongside rack

shipments and the higher content value of Vera Rubin. After the deal's completion, the
consolidation of Interplex should further expand the HPC sales contribution and drive
further margin expansion. Meanwhile, Bizlink has also identified opportunities in optical
connections through various partnerships. Earnings contributions from XFS are growing
robustly, though they remain a small proportion of the total. ALC and other CPO
revenue might not  contribute to earnings growth until H227, at the earliest.

Expect stronger HPC sales growth and margin expansion
Bizlink attributes the MoM sales decline in August to the summer holidays at its
European factories, which account for around one-third of capacity  and mainly supply
automation and industrial products. Management highlighted the historical patterns of
MoM improvements in September. Management remains positive about HPC and
capital equipment sales growth in the remainder of 2026. Data cables shipments have

recovered meaningfully since June. Power cables are growing rapidly with shipments of
Rubin servers, which have a much higher content value per rack than Blackwell. Further
upside could come from shipment of stand alone power side cars. The consolidation of
Interplex would serve as an additional growth driver after the deal is closed before end
of 2026. A higher sales mix from HPC could also drive gross margin expansion.
Engaging in various partnerships to capture optic interconnect opportunities

Management outlined several potential opportunities in optical connections: Credo's
ALC and other Micro-LED consortium products. These products provide mid-to-short
distance optical interconnection solutions. Credo plans to hold a demonstration in
October 2026, and Bizlink is the exclusive supplier. On CPO, Bizlink performs  fibre
assembly and supplies MPO connectors. It collaborates with FAU companies, including
Senko, and is working on solutions for shuffle boxes.

Valuation: Buy, price target at NT$3,617
We have a Buy rating with price target of NT$3,617, based on 30x 2027E PE.

Company Description
Founded in 1996, BizLink is headquartered in Fremont, California. BizLink provides
interconnect solutions, including connectors, harnesses and cables for a wide range of
industries, such as industrials, automotive, IT & data communications, and electrical

appliances. BizLink has 34 production facilities located in Asia, America and Europe.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
Our price target is based on a PE multiple.
The key company-specific risks are: 1) a global economic slowdown impacting end-demand;
2) a slower-than-expected change in the product mix leading to slower-than-expected
gross margin expansion; and 3) a rise in raw material prices.
The key industry-specific risks are: unexpected changes in the underlying global macro

environment, currency and interest rate movement and commodity price inflation.

KEY DEFINITIONS:Forecast Stock Return (FSR) is defined as expected percentage price appreciation plus gross dividend yield over
the next 12 months. In some cases, this yield may be based on accrued dividends. Market Return Assumption (MRA) is defined as
the one-year local market interest rate plus 5% (a proxy for, and not a forecast of, the equity risk premium). Under Review (UR)
Stocks may be flagged as UR by the analyst, indicating that the stock's price target and/or rating are subject to possible change in the

near term, usually in response to an event that may affect the investment case or valuation. Equity Price T argets have an investment
horizon of 12 months.

the relevant offering materials for that investment. Structured investments are unsecured obligations of a particular issuer with returns linked to the performance of an
underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

ab 18 September 2026
Global Research
First Read
Accton Technology Corporation
GM headwind should be lifted from Q426E
Revenue growth  remains on track despite component  consignment transition
We met  with Accton  earlier this week. Management remains confident that both Sept.
and Q426F sales will increase sequentially, supported by strong  demand for 800G
switches and the ramp-up of AI cards (i.e. Trainium 3), despite the transition of certain
components (memory and PCB) to a consignment model. We  estimate the consignment

shift reduced   Aug. sales by ~5%  and now forecast Q326E sales of NT$122.5 bn, up
28% QoQ (vs  prior +30% QoQ). Accton noted  it had prepaid for the higher-cost
components on behalf of  customers in the recent months to secure  supply availability,
but discussion regarding the reimbursement terms  remain ongoing. Given the timing
mismatch, its conservative accounting approach, and a higher sales mix from AI card, we
expect Q326E GM to decline 1.4 ppt QoQ to 18.3%, while OPM should remain relatively

resilient  on operating leverage. We forecast Q326E EPS of NT$25.39, up 29% QoQ.
GM recovery likely  from Q426E with higher content from liquid cooling
We forecast Q426E sales growth of 3% QoQ, supported by continued strength in  800G
switches and the ongoing ramp of Trainium 3. We expect one of the Trainium 3 models
will migrate from air cooled to liquid-cooled design, which carry ~20% higher ASP and
better GM due to increased design complexity. To strength its competitive positioning

and capture more value add,  Accton is expanding its in-house manufacturing
capabilities for the liquid-cooling components at its Malaysia facility. We expect liquid-
cooling adoption to accelerate across both Trainium 3 and next-gen Trainium 4, for
which we believe all models will adopt liquid cooling, given  better heat dissipation,
along with improving quality/yield for liquid cooling components.
Multiple drivers supporting 2027E growth
We see several catalysts supporting continued  growth into 2027E. Key drivers include:

(1) further Trainium 3 ramp with higher ASP for liquid cooling, (2) sustained 800G switch
demand with adoption of  new  platforms based on Marvell and Spectrum chipsets, (3)
migration to 1.6T switch, and (4) increasing  contribution from Optical Switch. We expect
its AI card business will grow ~50% YoY  in 2027E, after ~45% growth in 2026E, while
revenue contribution from social media customer to increase from low-teens % of sales
this year to mid-teens % in 2027E. Beyond existing customers, it is engaging with

additional  CSPs for potential 2027 pilot and the  L11 server rack has started initial
shipments in 2026, which should see more contribution in 2027E.
Valuation:Reiterate Buy with PT of NT$3,688
We lower  2026E EPS by 2%  but raise 2027-28E EPS by 2-3% to reflect the temporary
GM headwind offset by  higher contribution from liquid cooling AI card business. We
retain Buy rating with PT of NT$3,688, based on 26x average 2027-28E PE.  We believe
recent concern on component shortages and  lower margin on higher component cost is

overdone as we believe Accton's GM should gradually recover from Q426E.

Company Description
Founded in 1988, Accton specialises in ODM/OEM solutions for data center switches, AI
accelerator cards, enterprise/ODM switches, carrier access/telecom and others. Accton is one
of the largest vendors of white-box and OCP-compliant switches globally (by sales).

Leveraging deep expertise in high-speed switching, system integration and rapid time-to-
market, it has secured long-term partnerships with major cloud service providers.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Accton using PE methodology.
Key risks include: 1) weaker-than-expected demand for data center switches; 2) slower ramp
of 800G and 1.6T data center switches; 3) market share loss in the AI accelerator card
business; and 4) softer gross margin than expected.

to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ

## Document 113: 260921_daiwa_winway

Source PDF: all report pdf/260921_daiwa_winway.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-21
Pages: 7
Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

Taiwan Information Technology

What’s new: We provide an update on Winway’s business outlook.

What’s the impact: Marked revenue upside, but a more conservative 
gross margin outlook. We raise our 3Q26 revenue forecast by 9.3% to 
TWD5.0bn (+177.8% YoY) to reflect the stronger-than-expected execution 
of capacity expansion at Renwu Phase 1. Management guided for flat QoQ 
revenue in 4Q26, due to: 1) seasonality; 2) existing capacity being nearly 
fully utilised, with additional capacity scheduled to come online in 1H27; 
and 3) potential revenue recognition delays into 1H27 to accommodate 
customers’ schedules. On profitability, we lower our 3Q26E gross margin 
by 1.8pp, as we expect higher revenue contribution from probe cards and 
incremental depreciation from the new plant to dilute margins. Overall, for 
2026E and 2027E, we raise our revenue by 3.2% and 0.9%, while lowering 
our gross margin by 1.2pp and 1.7pp, respectively.

Probe card share concerns appear overdone. In response to concerns 
over probe card order losses, we believe the expanding TAM will attract 
competitors; the key differentiator is whether suppliers can scale capacity 
to meet customers’ demands. Winway does not expect its probe card share 
at its largest customer to decline and remains confident in maintaining its 
market-leading position. Its Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) 
probe card supply agreement with Technoprobe (TPRO IM, Not Rated) 
remains in place, which should support its technology competitiveness.

Socket capacity expansion remains on track. Winway doubled its socket 
capacity YoY in 2026 and remains on track to reach monthly pogo-pin 
capacity of 14m units by 1H27, per management. We estimate monthly 
capacity to grow further to 16-18m units by end-2027. Management’s long-
term target is to raise its pogo-pin self-sufficiency ratio to 50-60%, which 
should support gross margin expansion through greater vertical integration.

What we recommend: We slightly raise revenue top-line but lower our 
2026-28E EPS by 1-5% to factor in conservative gross margin 
assumptions. We reaffirm our Buy (1) call, with 12M TP of TWD10,000, 
based on a PER of 50x, applied to our 2027E forward EPS. Our 2026-28E 
EPS CAGR of 100% makes our target PER undemanding, given that the 
resulting PEG ratio is 0.5x. Key downside risks: intensifying competition.

How we differ: Our revised 2026-27E EPS are now roughly in line with 
consensus, reflecting a more prudent gross margin. While market noise 
persists, we see no structural threat to Winway's leading position in sockets 
and probe cards.

21 September 2026

Capacity ramp drives revenue upside

➢ Revenue upside with more prudent gross margin assumptions 
➢ Probe card position intact; socket expansion on track 
➢ Reaffirming Buy (1) rating with an unchanged 12M TP of TWD10,000

Company profile 
Founded in Kaohsiung in 2001, WinWay has evolved from an optoelectronic test-fixture supplier into a 
leading logic test-interface provider. Its portfolio includes test sockets, MEMS probe cards and contact 
elements. Growth is driven by increasing AI/HPC testing complexity, GPU and ASIC design wins, 
expanding SLT adoption and next-generation HyperSocket solutions.

Wiwynn (6669.TW): New ASIC and GPU AI server racks in expansion; 
Aug strong beat; TP up to NT$3,777; Buy
21 September 2026 | 6:21AM HKT
Wiwynn delivered strong Aug revenues, which were 27% ahead of our estimates, 
reflecting strong general servers demand from US leading CSPs, and its major 
customers’ new ASIC AI servers ramping up. We expect sequential revenues growth 
to continue through Dec 2026, leading 3Q26 / 4Q26 revenues to grow at +46% / 
+22% QoQ, driven by (1) major customers’ new ASIC AI servers ramping up, across 
air-cooled and liquid-cooled, (2) general servers end demand remaining solid on 
agentic AI, (3) new GPU-powered AI server racks entering mass production in 4Q26 
across NVIDIA and AMD platforms, and (4) potential new customers in ASIC AI 
servers. Maintain Buy with TP raised to NT$3,777 (21.5x 2027E P/E vs. +32% EPS YoY 
in 2027-28E).

Ongoing capacity expansion: As we highlighted in Aug (report link), Wiwynn 
announced a 2H26 capex budget of US$942m, implying 2026 capex could be up to 
NT$40bn (US$1.3bn). On Sep 16, the company announced equipment procurement 
of US$16m (NT$512m), reflecting the strong AI demand and the company’s 
commitments on capacity expansion. We estimate the company’s capex at NT$44bn 
in 2026E, and to stay at a similar high level through 2028E, supporting its production 
sites diversification across the US, Mexico, and Malaysia, AI servers expansion from 
ASIC to GPU-powered, and products expansion across different ASICs and GPUs, 
along with further customers penetration. 
Earnings revision: We factor in August revenues, and change our net income by +7% 
/ +5% / +3% in 2026-28E. The change is mainly on revenues: we raise 2026-28E 
revenues by 8% / 7% / 5%, reflecting the strong beat of Aug revenues driven by

Price Target Risks and Methodology - Wiwynn 
We are Buy-rated on Wiwynn with a 12-month TP of NT$3,777. Our target price is 
based on 21.5x 2027E P/E, which is derived from PC/server peers’ EPS growth vs. P/E 
multiple correlation. We see EPS growth as a major factor for the stock’s performance. 
Key downside risks: 1) weaker-than-expected AI server demand growth; 2) 
slower-than-expected recovery in general server demand; and 3) more severe 
competition in the server ODM market.

TV panel prices stayed flat MoM in September: Mainstream 32", 43", 55", 65" and
75" TV panel prices all stood flat for the month of September,  in line with our
expectations. While the overall TV panel demand was lackluster, there is still some
seasonal demand as brands are preparing for year-end promotions. Recently, the
major Chinese panel makers have notified their customers of price hikes from

September/October in order to mitigate increasing margin pressure caused by rising
costs of various components, including driver ICs, glass substrates and PCB.
Although major Chinese panel makers might leverage their annual maintenance of
three to seven days during October 2026 as a bargaining chip, we think it might take
more negotiations with brand customers before they can really raise panel prices,
since order momentum will slow down in the coming months. On a quarterly

average basis, TV panel prices  declined in the low-single-digits % QoQ in 3Q26.
IT panel prices were flat MoM in  September: Monitor and notebook panel prices
stayed flat MoM during the month. Both applications continues to  see slower
demand in  2H26 post the earlier restocking  in 1H26 amid concerns about  increasing
component costs. That said, panel makers are under cost pressure and reluctant to
given more price concessions. On a quarterly average basis, we expect IT panel

prices to remain flat QoQ in 3Q26.
Risk/reward less attractive: We think that the current valuation of Taiwanese panel
makers, AUO (2409.TW) and Innolux (3481.TW) both at 1.7x P/B, has already baked
in some expectations of glass in advanced packaging for revenue contribution in
2028. However, some supply chain players think this might take longer, and there
seem to be more suppliers from different supply chains vying for this opportunity. In
China, while expectations are also building for the glass core substrate, we have a

relative preference for BOE (000725.SZ; 1.5x P/B) over TCL (000100.SZ; 1.8x P/B),
on its scale advantage and faster progress in glass core substrates.

TV Panel Prices Trending Down from 3Q26
TV panel prices started to edge up at the beginning of this year, rising 1% MoM in January,
2% MoM in February and 2% MoM in March. April, May and June were largely flat, while
July was down 2% MoM, August was down 1% MoM, and September was flat MoM,   in line
with our expectation that TV panel prices would start trending down from 3Q26.  That
said, we do not expect a significant decline as supply-side discipline should provide

downside support.

Below-seasonal Panel Shipments in 2H26
Over the past decade, TV panel shipments have typically been split 49%:51% between 1H
and 2H. In 2026, we expect the mix to skew toward 1H, as TV brands restocked ahead of
major promotional events, including the Winter Olympics in February, the FIFA World Cup
in June-July, and China's 618 shopping festival. We see no clear evidence that these events

will materially boost global TV demand, but they have historically shifted shipment timing
across quarters. As a result, we expect the restocking momentum seen since the start of
the year to fade, with panel order momentum slowing in 2H26.
Display Fab Utilization  at ~85% in 3Q26
Stronger TV panel shipments supported display fab utilization of ~80% in 4Q24 and 82%
in 1Q25. Utilization declined to 78% in 2Q25 as brands adopted a more cautious stance

following earlier pull-ins and as the impact of China's trade-in program moderated.
Utilization rebounded to 80-85% in 3Q25 as brands restocked for year-end promotions
and remained at similar levels in 4Q25 despite seasonal softness as well as in 1Q26.
Industry utilization stayed broadly flat QoQ, at 80-85% in 2Q26, reflecting continued
supply discipline, followed by a slight uptick in 3Q26.
Over the medium to long term, we continue to believe the display industry is undergoing

structural change. Chinese panel makers have shifted their focus from top-line growth to
profitability, while lower government subsidies have reinforced supply discipline. We
believe investors increasingly recognize that the industry's production-to-order model can
remain sustainable, particularly as panel price cycles shortened to quarters in 2023-24 vs.
multiyear cycles in the previous decade. Consolidation actions, including LG Display's sale
of its Gen 8.5 Guangzhou fab to TCL and Sharp's closure of its Gen 10 Sakai fab, also

Changes on Supply Side Not Fairly Priced In, June 17, 2021).

Risk/Reward Fair After Recent Correction
We view risk-reward as broadly balanced following the recent correction in panel stocks.
Below are our current views:
• AUO (2409.TW, Derrick Yang): We rate AUO Equal-weight with a PT of NT
$27.00, based on a 1.4x 2026e P/B multiple. While we believe the current round of
TV panel price increases is nearing an end, major panel makers should continue to
demonstrate solid supply discipline, providing downside support. We appreciate

AUO's efforts to diversify its business, but meaningful earnings contributions are
likely to take time.
• BOE (000725.SZ, Derrick Yang): We prefer BOE due to its scale advantage,
higher exposure to display and faster progress in glass core substrates. Our PT of
Rmb9.30 is based on 2.5x 2026e P/B, which we view as reasonable given our
estimated ROE of 5-8% over 2026-28 compared with BOE's average P/B of 1.1x and
ROE of 2-4% during 2023-25.
• Innolux (3481.TW, Derrick Yang): In semiconductors, our supply-chain checks

suggest that Innolux is participating in a foundry customer's glass core substrate
project. However, we do not expect meaningful contributions before 2028, and
additional competitors could enter as the industry moves toward mass production.
We maintain our Equal-weight rating and PT of NT$60.00, based on a 2.1x 2026e
P/B multiple.
• LG Display (034220.KS, Ryan Kim): Meaningful OLED revenue contribution
should increasingly improve earnings from 2H25, but potentially weaker end-

markets keep us from turning bullish on LGD. The stock trades at 0.6x 2026e P/B
vs. a historical mid-cycle level of 0.5x.
• TCL (000100.SZ, Derrick Yang): We are EW with a price target of Rmb4.70 (1.7x
2026e P/B). The stock is trading at 1.8x 2026e P/B vs. its mid-cycle average of 1.4x
since 2022.
• Greater China DDIC supply chain implications – Novatek (3034.TW, Daniel Yen):
Our Underweight thesis reflects weaker PC, smartphone and automotive demand,

gross margin pressure, and a lack of new growth drivers. That said, Novatek's
OLED DDI roadmap appears more competitive than those of its key Korean peers
in terms of both performance and cost, helping it gain share in Apple's iPhone
supply chain.

Where We Could Be Wrong
• Stronger end demand: If end demand for major applications turns out to be better
than expected, there could be stronger panel shipments and less panel price
pressure.
• More stringent output control: If major panel makers collectively adjust
utilization to an extreme extent, they could mitigate pricing pressure in the case of
softer demand.
• Non-commodity display business: If the non-commodity business progresses

faster than expected, panel makers could show better financial results.

健鼎(3044 TT)  
台灣股市︱電子上游 
投 資 速 報 
買進-維持 目標價 NT$654 (潛在報酬+30.0%) 2026-09-11

伺服器與記憶體雙刀流   
◼ 結 論 與 建 議 
毛利率與營益率同步創高，核心動能來自高階產品比重提升與折舊負擔下
降，中長期則受惠高階 PCB 需求成長與產品組合優化。預估健鼎 (3044 
T T)2026 年 EPS  31.01 元， 2027 年 隨 湖 北 、 越 南 產 能 開 出 ， 月產能朝 100
億 元 以 上 推 進 ， 支 撐 營 收 持 續 成 長，EPS 38.48 元， 建 議 給 予 本 益 比 17 倍，
設定目標價 654 元（ 17X ＊ 2027(F )） ， 評 等 「 買 進 」 。

◼ 重點摘要  
AI HP C 趨勢 帶 動 新 型 記 憶 體 架 構 需 求  
PCB 過 去 主 要 成 長 動 能 來 自 手 機 等 消 費 性 電 子 ， 但 隨 AI 與 資 料 中 心 需 求 興
起 ， 伺 服 器 、 網 通 與 高 速 運 算 應 用 成 為 重 要 支 撐 。 隨 平 台 升 級 （ 如 DD R5 、
PCIe Gen5 ） 帶 動 資 料 傳 輸 速 度 提 升 ， 對 高 多 層 板 與 部 分 HDI 產 品 的 需 求
同 步 增 加 ， 產 品 規 格 與 層 數 亦 持 續 提 升 。 此 外 ， 高 階 應 用 比 重 提 升 有 助 於
產 品 組 合 優 化 ， 帶 動 單 價 與 附 加 價 值 提 升 ； 同 時 ， 隨 系 統 架 構 與 高 速 傳 輸
需 求 演 進 ， PCB 在 系 統 中 的 重 要 性 持 續 提 高 。 整 體 而 言 ， 高 多 層 板 為 主 要
成 長 動 能 ， HDI 則 在 特 定 應 用 中 維 持 穩 定 需 求 。 另 在 低 軌 衛 星 等 新 興 應 用
中 ， 對 高 可 靠 度 與 高 密 度 板 需 求 逐 步 提 升 ， 也 帶 來 潛 在 發 展 機 會 。

        單位：百萬元

公 司 簡 介 ─ 全 球 前 十 大 P CB 廠 之 一  
健鼎科技初期主要從事 POS 系 統 之 產 銷 及 週 邊 設 計 ， 1996 年 成 立 印 刷 電 路
板（ PCB ）事 業 部 後 逐 步 轉 型 為 專 業 PCB 製 造 廠 。 主 要 產 品 為 雙 面 板 與 多 層
板 ， 終 端 應 用 涵 蓋 記 憶 體 模 組 、 薄 膜 電 晶 體 液 晶 顯 示 器 （ TFT -LCD ）、硬
碟、伺服器 / 工作 站 、 汽 車 電 子 、 筆 記 型 電 腦 及 行 動 電 話 等 多 元 領 域 。 PCB
作為電子零組件連接與訊號 傳輸的核心載體，依層數區分為單 層板、雙層
板與多層板，其中多層板為公司主要產品線。原物料包括基板、銅箔、樹
脂、金鹽、乾膜、磷銅球與油墨等化學材料。 生 產 據 點 涵 蓋 台 灣 平 鎮 廠 ，
以 及 中 國 江 蘇 無 錫 I 、 II 廠與湖北仙桃廠，並持續推進越南邊和廠布局。

Ser ver 與 Module 出 貨 增 加  
健鼎 2Q2026 營收 248.6 億元， QoQ +18.6% ， YoY +38.8% ，毛利率
30.1% ， QoQ +3.6ppts ， YoY +3.9ppts ，營益率 22.5% ， QoQ 
+4.1ppts ， YoY +4.5ppts ， EPS 7.41 元 。 毛 利 率 改 善 主 要 來 自 產 品 組 合 優
化 、 營 收 放 大 與 折 舊 率 下降 。 預估 健鼎 3Q2026 營收 302.9 億 元 ， QoQ 
+21.8% ， YoY +56.2% ， 毛 利 率 30.3% ， QoQ +0.2ppts ， YoY +3.5ppts ，
營益率 22.7% ， QoQ +0.2ppts ， YoY +4.1ppts ， EPS 9.14 元。 3Q26 營收
維持成長，主要受惠 Ser ver 與 Module 出 貨 增 加 ； 毛 利 率 有 望 維 持 30% 以
上 ， 費 用 率 控 制 於 8.0% 左右，全年營收挑戰 1,000 億元。

表二 、 全球 PCB 製 造 產 值 與成長 趨勢

資料 來源 ： 公 司 ， 康 和 投 顧 整 理 。

客戶涵蓋歐美及亞洲大型客戶  
公 司 客 戶 涵 蓋 國 際 一 線 品 牌 與 系 統 廠 ， 應 用 橫 跨 記 憶 體 模 組 （ DDR4 、
DDR5 ）、 硬 碟 、 筆 記 型 電 腦 、 光 電 板 、 手 機 、 AI 伺服器與車電等領域；目
前 產 品 組 合 以 Ser ver 為 主 ， 占 營 收 約 42% ， 其 次 為 DRAM/SSD 23% 、
Automotive 16% 等 ，隨 Ser ver 與 Modul e 需求持續成長， 2H26 兩 者 合 計
營 收 占 比 可 望 超 過 70% ， 帶 動 高 階 多 層 板 與 高 可 靠 度 產 品 出 貨 提 升 。 此
外，公司深耕車用、伺服器與工業等高可靠度應用，具 規模與製造優勢 。

強化高階板比重  
2026 持 續 擴 充 湖 北 、 越 南 產 能 ， 1H26 資 本 支 出 約 71.9 億 元 ， 全 年 規 劃 約
150 億 元 ， 越 南 新 廠 預 計 4Q26 小量量 產； 2027 年 月 產 能 朝 100 億元以上
發展，全年營收挑戰 1,200 億元 。產品端以 General Ser ver 大量出貨為基
礎，逐 步 提 升 AI 與 高 階 HDI 比 重，目 前 Ser ver 中約 10 ～ 15% 為 AI 相 關 板、
約 10% 為 HDI 產 品 ， 已 具 二 、 三 階 HDI 製 程 能 力 。

地緣政治與供應鏈重組，需求穩健復甦  
公司產能以中國無錫與湖北為核心，越南為擴產與分散地緣風險據點 ，其中
周德新廠 2026 年 第 一 季 試 產 ， 月 產 能 約 30 萬 呎，以 NB 與 伺 服 器 板 為 主 。
在地緣政治與供應鏈重組趨勢下，客戶對於生產基地多元化的需求提升 ，公
司亦配合客戶需求進行海外產能布局。 全球 PCB 產業仍以中國為主要生產
基 地 （ 市 占 56% 至 57% ） ， 中 國 廠 商 （ 如 勝 宏 ） 持 續 擴 產 下 ， 不 過 ， 同 時 供
應鏈外移趨勢延續，泰國與越南將成為後續產能布局重點。

欣銓 (3264 TT)  Buy

晶圓大廠新訂單逐步向上，建議 Buy。  
投資建議 ：欣銓 2026 年資本支出轉向積極擴張，主要來自與策
略客戶已確定之 ASIC 合作案。欣銓 1H26 在取得不動產、廠房
及設備的現金流出達新台幣 70.07 億元，較 1H25 的 18.65 億元
大幅增加約 51.4 億元。預期 2H26 則隨龍潭廠機台陸續交付並
完成數據驗證後，進入產能爬坡期，營收逐步向上。在排除匯
率波動前提下 ， 獲利亦預計維持逐季成長的趨勢 。 預估欣銓2026
年稅後 EPS 9.94 元。龍潭廠新專案是 2026~2027 年最重要的增
長引擎 。 公司與策略夥伴(晶圓廠 )合作的 ASIC 測試專案 07/2026
開始明顯增加，而旗下全智湖口新廠，也於 3Q26 正式進入矽光
子相關新產品的量產階段，都將帶動公司中長期營收獲利向上，
因此建議欣銓 Buy ，目標價 322 元 (2027 年 PER24X) 。  
2Q26 稅後 EPS 2.36 元： AI 相關需求佳和通訊相關訂單維持強
勁。欣銓 2Q26 營收為 45.34 億元， QoQ+13.81% 。營收依應用
別分析，通訊 Communication/Connectivity 佔 33.4% ；車用 /安控
(ATV/Security) 佔 18.2% ；射頻晶片 (RF IC) 佔 12.2% ；微處理器
(General MCU) 佔 8.5% ； Storage 佔 10.8% ； PC/Consumers 佔
9.9% ；Memory 佔 5.4% ；其他 1.6% 。毛利率的部份， 2Q26 毛利
率為 40.17% ，增加 1.81 個百分點。 2Q26 稅後 EPS 2.36 元。  
預估 3Q26 稅後 EPS 2.73 元：龍潭新廠歷經 1H26 客戶驗證與
進場裝機後，已於 07/2026 起正式進入量產階段，帶動欣銓
08/2026 營收增加至 17.94 億元， MoM+1.57% ， YoY+46.57% 。
此廠區主要與晶圓代工廠 (Foundry) 合作，針對  AI ASIC 提供
測試服務。這批高階機台目前的稼動率極高，幾乎處於滿載狀
態，其量產將顯著貢獻 3Q26 營收，也會讓晶圓代工業務的營收
佔比在 3Q26 逐漸放大。此外，在傳統應用領域如車用 IC 及  
General MCU 方面 ， 由於客戶端在疫後的庫存已降至合理水位 ，
需求正逐步回升。預估 3Q26 稅後 EPS 2.73 元。

6 群益投顧 
  【投資評等說明】  
  評等  定義  
  強力買進 (Strong Buy)  首次評等潛在上漲空間 ≥ 35%  
  買進 (Buy)  15% ≤首次評等潛在上漲空間 <35%  
  區間操作 (Trading Buy) 5% ≤首次評等潛在上漲空間 <15%

中立 (Neutral)  
無法由基本面給予投資評等  
預期近期股價將處於盤整  
建議降低持股

【投資評等調整機制】  
  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月
目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。   
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：  
1.  達目標價。  
2.  雖未達原訂目標價，但檢視基本面、訊息面、籌碼面等多方訊息，研
判股價上漲空間已然有限，將適時出具降評報告。  
3.  推薦後股價不漲反跌。

【免責聲明】  
  本研究報告僅提供予特定人之客戶作為參考資料「非經同意不得轉載」 。我
們並不確保此資訊的完整性與正確性，投資人應了解，報告中有關未來預測
之陳述可能不會實現，因而不應被依賴。而且此報告並非根據特定投資目的
或依預定對象之財務狀況所撰寫出來的，因此，此研究報告的目的，既非對
投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提供詢價服
務，亦非作為進行交易的要約。投資人應注意到相關證券之價值及收益，可
能會有無預警地上升或下降，產生投資回報金額可能比原始投資來得少的
情形。
